body.statement: For either \(r=\mathrm{SDC}\) or \(r=\mathrm{LEI}\), every \(Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\) induces, for each arm \(a\), a sign \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\) and missing-cell means \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) such that \(\theta_a(Q)=c_a+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_jx_{a,j}\). Conversely, every vector in \(\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\) is realized by a bounded missing-cell completion satisfying the branch score inequalities; exact aggregate support is addressed by Theorem 1.
body.justification: This is the finite-dimensional reduction that separates moment feasibility from full-support completion.
body.gap: BanKedagni2022 derives valid inequalities but does not identify the missing-cell completion polytope or prove a converse.
body.consumer: Every later endpoint, support, and computation result reduces to this finite object.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(C=(D,Z)\).  By Assumption \(\text{ass:finite-grid}\), \(C=c_j\) has probability \(p_j>0\), and the cells in \(\mathcal J\) exhaust the support of \(C\).  Fix \(a\in\{d,e\}\) and \(Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\), and put
\[
 \bar y_{a,j}=\mathbb E_Q[Y_a\mid C=c_j].
\]
The bounded support in the definition of \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\) makes every conditional expectation finite.  Compatibility and consistency give \(\bar y_{a,j}=m_j\) for \(j\in\mathcal O_a\).  Set \(x_{a,j}=\bar y_{a,j}\) for \(j\in\mathcal M_a\).  The support restriction gives \(x_{a,j}\in[\ell_a,u_a]\), and finite-cell iterated expectation gives
\[
 \theta_a(Q)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}p_j\bar y_{a,j}
 =c_a+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_jx_{a,j}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
Because every score is constant within a cell and is centered under \(P\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Q[s_C^rY_a]
 =h_a^r+\sum_{j\in\mathcal M_a}p_js_j^rx_{a,j}.                                 \tag{2}
\]
For SDC, the two coordinates of (2) are \(\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_a,D)\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_a,Z)\).  Two real numbers \(v_1,v_2\) satisfy \(v_1v_2\ge0\) if and only if there is \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\) with \(bv_1\ge0\) and \(bv_2\ge0\): choose the common sign when both are nonzero and choose the sign of the nonzero coordinate when one is zero.

For LEI, Assumption \(\text{ass:target-overlap}\), together with \(d\ne e\), implies \(\sigma_D>0\), while Assumption \(\text{ass:lei-scale}\) gives \(\sigma_Z>0\).  If
\[
 A=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_a,D)}{\sigma_D},\qquad
 B=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_Q(Y_a,Z)}{\sigma_Z},
\]
then the coordinates of (2) are \(B\) and \(A-B\).  Moreover,
\[
 AB\ge0\ \text{ and }\ |A|\ge|B|
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists b\in\{-1,+1\}:\ bB\ge0\ \text{ and }\ b(A-B)\ge0.                  \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the left side permits choosing the common sign of \(A\) and \(B\); conversely, the right side gives \(bA=bB+b(A-B)\ge bB\ge0\), hence common sign and \(|A|\ge|B|\).  Equations (2)--(3) and Assumption \(\text{ass:correlation-restriction}\) therefore yield a branch sign \(b\) for which \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\).  Together with (1), this proves the forward reduction.

Conversely, take \(x_a\in\mathcal F_{a,b}^r(P)\).  Draw \((Y,D,Z)\) from \(P\).  On a cell with \(D=a\), set \(Y_a=Y\); on cell \(j\in\mathcal M_a\), let \(Y_a=x_{a,j}\) deterministically.  The latter variables are bounded by \([\ell_a,u_a]\), compatibility is unchanged, and consistency holds on the factual cells.  Equations (1) and (2) now follow by direct conditioning, and membership in the polytope is exactly the coordinatewise branch inequality.  Unrestricted potential outcomes for other arms can be adjoined on independent auxiliary uniforms.  This converse asserts bounded-range and branch-score feasibility only; the additional exact aggregate-support requirement is proved separately in \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\).
